meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'swimming pool' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always swimming pool.

examples.text: Безусловно, вам нужен полный покой и отдых.
examples.trans: Without a doubt, you need complete peace and rest.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно безусловно и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite without a doubt and calmly.

meanings.note: medical institution for inpatient care

examples.trans: Everyone thinks you're in the hospital.
He was admitted to the hospital.

examples.text: Все думают, ты в больнице. Откуда деньги?
examples.trans: Everyone thinks you're in the hospital. Where did the money come from?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.trans: A big city.
The sum is very large.

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wake up'.

examples.trans: It is useless to wake him.

examples.text: А вдруг мы его разбудим? И у него начнутся боли?
examples.trans: What if we wake him up? And what if his pains start?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.
What delicious tea!

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'together' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We're together.
We live together.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: the invisible gas substance of atmosphere
Outdoor environment. Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'здух'). Common masculine noun meaning 'air; outdoors' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Успокойся, пойдём на свежий воздух сейчас.
examples.trans: Calm down, let us go outside into fresh air now.

examples.text: Я просто стою и дышу воздухом.
examples.trans: I am just standing and breathing air.

meanings.note: after a plural noun or pronoun: вы все
Всем = to everyone (dative). Core Russian pron meaning 'all; everyone' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You're all thieves.
Nobody cares.

examples.text: И знаешь, что самое главное? Всем всё равно.
examples.trans: And you know the main thing? Nobody cares.

вставать.gloss: to get up, to stand up

meanings.note: Out of bed or from the floor. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тавать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to get up, to stand up', paired with 'встать'.
Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тавать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to get up, to stand up', paired with 'встать'.

examples.trans: Come on, Tuzik, let's get up!
I get up at seven in the morning.
Come on, Tuzik, let's get up!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'town, city' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I love our town.
It's a small town.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.
This is indeed an important question.
Quiet, stop! It really hurts!

meanings.note: About people. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind; good').
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.trans: Good evening!
She is very kind.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I'm thinking about work.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.
I want to live normally.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!

meanings.note: Morning meal. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втрак'). Common masculine noun meaning 'breakfast' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.

meanings.note: From замечательный. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'мечательно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Well, that is wonderful!
We had a wonderful rest.

examples.text: Так это замечательно! Раньше вы чувствовали ко мне отвращение.
examples.trans: Well, that is wonderful! Before, you felt disgust toward me.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Чн is pronounced шн. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strong, sturdy, firm').

examples.text: Рука у тебя крепкая, как у деда.
examples.trans: Your grip is strong, just like your grandfather's.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'bed' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is my bed.
Foot on the bed.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: Locative в лесу after в/на. Common masculine noun meaning 'forest, woods' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Давайте поедем в лес на шашлыки! Даню вон с собой возьмём.

examples.trans: Look, Uncle Danya has gone pale, see! He is afraid of the winter forest.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'horses / horsepower' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

находиться.gloss: to be located, to be found

meanings.en: to be located, to be situated
meanings.note: Imperfective reflexive verb. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ходиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be located, to be found', paired with 'найтись'.

examples.trans: Where is the operating room located?

examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job

examples.trans: I need a job too.
Do you need a pen?
He needs money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'становка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'atmosphere / setting' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы пытаемся создавать тут особую тёплую обстановку.
examples.trans: We are trying to create a special warm atmosphere here.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть обстановка.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always atmosphere.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'rest' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You definitely need to get a good rest right now.

examples.text: Так что иди спокойно домой и отдохни.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'стирать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'washed everything'.

examples.text: Макс, я собрала все твои вещи, перестирала, погладила.
examples.trans: Max, I packed all your things, washed and ironed them.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и перестирать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and washed everything on time.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Здравствуйте. Оставьте в покое Аллу Евгеньевну!
examples.trans: Hello. Leave Alla Yevgenyevna alone!

meanings.note: Полный кошмар = a total nightmare. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('full, complete, total').

Полный кошмар = a total nightmare. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('full, complete, total').

examples.trans: This is a total nightmare!

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.

meanings.note: + dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.trans: Maybe you could help?
Of course I'll help.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, wonderful').

A wonderful idea.

examples.text: Посмотри, какой у нас город прекрасный. Озёра, луга.
examples.trans: Look what a beautiful town we have. Lakes, meadows.

придумать.gloss: to think up, to come up with

meanings.en: to think up, to invent, to come up with
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think up, to come up with', paired with 'придумывать'.

examples.text: Как нет? Ты же сам это всё придумал!
examples.trans: What do you mean, no time? You came up with all this yourself!

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'm just tired.
It's easy.

meanings.note: Прямо так = just like that. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: Рано умер = died young / too early. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: There is one good hospital, or rather a quiet sanatorium.

examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always sanatorium.

meanings.note: Food, air, news. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вежий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fresh').

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: What did you say?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'менить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to change / replace'.

examples.text: Ладно, можно один раз и сменить мебель.
examples.trans: Alright, we can replace the furniture just once.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и сменить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to change on time.

meanings.note: Видeть сон / снится сон. Common substantive noun meaning 'dream; sleep' in everyday Russian.
Common substantive noun meaning 'dream; sleep' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He's having terrible dreams.

examples.text: И так всю ночь! Ему снятся страшные сны.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
